title: Top three scores
hints: Small scores work and big ones don't. Try `[...[100, 25, 9]].sort()` on its own and look at the order you get.
Without arguments, `sort()` compares items as **text**, so `"100"` comes before `"25"` and `"9"` comes last. Numbers need a compare function.
Replace `.sort().reverse()` with `.sort((a, b) => b - a)`, which sorts numbers from biggest to smallest.
